questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The natur and opportunities in the natur

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think the guidance from KU and the guidance from UiT could have been significantly better. I have many times been in doubt whether there is something I am missing and whether I will get it all under control. The information about course that I could take was little and I was getting various information.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Little. I would have like to have more, and also more information when you are leaving. What to do next.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: At email, where most of the communication was done, it think that the tone was very rude. The period before my exchange was by that very stressful, I during my exchange I did not have any idea of where to get help. Is have to be improved.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think we did it a day in the introduction week, it was okay

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: A day in the introduction week. Okay, but it could have been more organisted

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was two people how could sign our arrival document

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
It was very difficult. I am studying Geografi og geoinformatik, where there are 4 spots 
specifically for geography at UiT. For me it was very difficult to be able to take 30 ECTS point with something around physical geography. When I arrived it was easier to get into course I over mail not was allowed to. So I have used a lot of time to get it to fit. With though on I probably not are the first gregograph to read in Tromsø and with a specific collaboration there, I had expected it to be easier and better.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Write emails to someone in the department that out are interested in. The email answer from the exchange coordinator was poorly and more opportunities was possible if you contacted direct.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I have learned a lot, but mostly through being in a new academic context rather than the courses specifically

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level fit quite well with the level in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
A bit the same. In one of my courses there was more home assignments and lab reports then I have been use to, but it was nice and a new learning for me. 
Nice that there also was group work and projects (Ocean climate)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I have been skiing a lot, and to go randonee skiing and spent time in the natur have been the biggest experience in my exchange. Go camping, go to a DNT cabin, go hiking. Tromsø is an amazing place to be in the natur.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Many was quite settled in their friendships. I spent a lot of time with other exchange studens, and I am very happy with that. Maybe it can be easier to become friends with locals in the fall semester.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That I could understand the language and the love for natur and outdoor experience.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Go skiing 
Go camping 
Rent a car sometimes to see more of the natur

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are going in the spring semester - go skiing. My friends who did not go randonee skiing regret it. It is the most easy way to be in natur, and there is so many opportunities. Join an avalanche course and buy the equipment usted at Finn or from new. It is expensive, but it can be usted at skiing tours or just to go to a cabin. In winter time it can be difficult to use the mountains without skies or snowshoes, and it is helpful and safely to have avalanche knowledge.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Skiing and improve my English skills.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To use English in an academic context, but it have been a good learning.

questions.answer: Yes
